# Contributing to FastAPI Doctor

Thank you for your interest in FastAPI Doctor. This document outlines the contribution guidelines for this project.

## Project Ownership

This repository is maintained by @guerschom1103. The repository owner has exclusive write access to the main branch.

## Contribution Workflow

### For Readers and Users
- You can read all code and documentation
- You can create issues to report bugs or request features
- You can fork the repository for personal use
- You can create pull requests for review (though only the owner can merge)

### For Contributors
1. Fork the repository
2. Create a feature branch
3. Make your changes
4. Add or update tests
5. Update documentation
6. Submit a pull request

## Code Standards

### Python Code
- Follow PEP 8 guidelines
- Use type hints for all function signatures
- Write comprehensive docstrings
- Keep functions focused and small

### Testing
- Write unit tests for new features
- Ensure existing tests pass
- Maintain test coverage
- Use descriptive test names

### Documentation
- Update README.md for user-facing changes
- Update DOCUMENTATION.md for technical changes
- Add comments for complex logic
- Keep documentation in sync with code

## Issue Reporting

When reporting issues:
1. Use the issue template
2. Provide reproduction steps
3. Include environment details
4. Add relevant code snippets
5. Specify expected vs actual behavior

## Pull Request Process

1. Ensure your code follows project standards
2. Update documentation as needed
3. Add tests for new functionality
4. Ensure all tests pass
5. Request review from @guerschom1103

## Review Process

All pull requests will be reviewed by @guerschom1103. The review process may include:
- Code quality assessment
- Security review
- Performance evaluation
- Documentation verification

## License

By contributing, you agree that your contributions will be licensed under the same MIT License that covers the project.

## Contact

For questions about contributions, contact @guerschom1103 through GitHub issues.

---

**Important:** This project follows a maintainer-driven development model. While contributions are welcome, final decisions on code changes, architecture, and project direction rest with the repository owner.
